Chapter 6: Making Choices When the Path Isn’t Clear
You know, life doesn’t come with a set of instructions. Most of the time, the choices we face are wrapped up in uncertainty—like what to say, who to trust, or which direction to take next. And if you take a closer look, the Bible is actually full of people standing at those same crossroads, just as unsure as we are about what’s around the corner.
The thing is, these stories don’t hand us a magic formula. But they do show us what it looks like to keep moving, even when the way ahead is foggy.
Imagine a student, staring at a college application, feeling the weight of every blank space. The pressure to pick the “right” path can feel overwhelming, can’t it? In moments like that, she remembers Abraham—called to leave everything familiar and head into the unknown. Abraham didn’t have a map. He just had a promise that he wouldn’t be walking alone.
That’s a quiet kind of comfort: sometimes, the most important step is simply the next one.
Then there’s another teen, wrestling with whether to speak up when a friend’s being bullied, or stay silent to avoid becoming a target himself. The story of Esther comes to mind: “For such a time as this.” Esther’s courage wasn’t about having all the answers—it was about showing up when it really mattered.
And that lesson sticks: most people wait for perfect clarity, but real life is shaped by choices that are brave, even when they’re messy.
Or think about the boy who’s always been the peacemaker, afraid to rock the boat. He reads about Jesus in the garden, wrestling with what’s ahead. Even Jesus, facing the toughest choice, asked if there could be another way. The honesty of that moment is powerful—because courage isn’t about being fearless; it’s about moving forward, even when you’re scared.
Sometimes, the hardest choices are about letting go. Maybe it’s a friendship that’s turned toxic, a dream that just doesn’t fit anymore, or an old grudge that’s stealing your peace. The Bible’s stories of forgiveness and new beginnings aren’t only about dramatic moments—they’re about the daily work of letting go. And little by little, you start to see that freedom isn’t about getting everything you want, but trusting that you’re being held, even when you don’t know how things will turn out.
Over time, these stories become less about finding the “right” answer and more about learning to listen—to God, to the people around you, and to that quiet voice inside. The path won’t always be clear, but the invitation is the same: keep walking, one step at a time, trusting that just enough light will show up for the next stretch of road.
